rationale: B wins because it is more assignment-ready: sharper sub-beats, tougher proof gates, and a real bottom-rung customer angle. Its best line, "Wise routes cross-border business payments around correspondent banking," is clean and testable; A's competing "direct shot at correspondent banking's toll booth" is good, but a shade more slogan than story. The margin is only slight because B also steps on a rake with "three days" and "minutes," which are not in the supplied facts.
gaps_in_A: "For a profitable public payments company, cutting correspondent-banking fees is a margin story" overreaches: cheaper for businesses is supplied, but Wise's own margin benefit is not.
"funding-mechanics" is the wrong label for the equities angle; this is public-company unit economics, not funding mechanics.
"evidence of other regulated payments/financial companies doing something comparable" makes the category angle depend on outside proof the update does not provide.
A spots the missing customer problem in "without one, the strongest concrete, ground-floor version of this story doesn't exist yet," but fails to turn that into a conditional customer-story angle.
gaps_in_B: "The businesses waiting three days for a payment that clears in minutes" invents timing the update does not give. The body asks for proof, but the headline has already made the claim.
"putting stablecoins on its balance-sheet flows" is too loaded; the update says businesses can hold and settle in stablecoin, not that Wise itself carries stablecoins on its balance sheet.
"the first time this flow is being described as a shipped feature rather than a position" is not in the update and should not be asserted blind.
The next step, `newsjack-detector`, is less direct than `journalist-fit-check` for a company-owned launch unless the team is explicitly trying to attach this to outside news.
